literal: Yesterday he was present, one person; today he is not, saying [this] greatness possesses this world.
translation: This world possesses the mighty reputation that a person who was alive yesterday is no more today.
modern: நேற்று இருந்த ஒருவன் இன்று இல்லை என்று சொல்லும் பெருமையை இந்த உலகம் பெற்றுள்ளது.
explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute transience of human life. The word 'perumai' (greatness or distinction) is used here with solemn irony to describe the world's defining power of impermanence. By contrasting 'nerunal' (yesterday) with 'iṉṟu' (today), the poet shows how quickly life can vanish. The greatness of this world lies in its constant reminder that no one, no matter how powerful, is guaranteed another day.
